title: Close AA pair at r = 0.5: is one power law with a scale enough inside r = 1?
pitch: Round 3 gives a scale s(r) on the P-0008 AA law: 0.61 at r = 1.0, 0.75 at 1.5, 0.92 at 2.5, about 1 at 3.5 to 4. Question: is the law still one power law times a scale at r = 0.5? Two A particles at rest 0.5 apart, T = 0.2, dt = 0.0001. Prediction: the pre-contact separation is fitted at noise by one scale s in 0.4 to 0.6, extrapolated from the trend. Falsifier: no single s gives chi2/n <= 2 over the pre-contact window, which would mean the law changes shape below r = 1.
